1. Functions of bounded variation

A function $u\in L^1(\Omega)$ on an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is of bounded variation when its distributional gradient is a finite vector-valued Radon measure: there exists $Du=(D_1u,\dots,D_nu)$, finite signed Borel measures, with

$$\int_\Omega u\,\partial_i\phi\,dx \;=\; -\int_\Omega \phi\,d(D_iu)\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C^1_c(\Omega).$$

The total variation $|Du|(\Omega)$ — the variation measure of the vector measure $Du$ — equals the dual norm

$$|Du|(\Omega)\;=\;\sup\Bigl\{\,\int_\Omega u\,\mathrm{div}\,\phi\,dx \,:\, \phi\in C^1_c(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n),\,|\phi(x)|\le 1\,\Bigr\}.$$

Why widen $W^{1,1}$ to $\mathrm{BV}$? Because $W^{1,1}$ requires the gradient measure to be absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, ruling out jumps. The Heaviside on $\mathbb{R}$ has $u'=\delta_0$ — a finite Radon measure but not in $L^1$ — so $H\in\mathrm{BV}_{\mathrm{loc}}\setminus W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Every BV function admits a Radon-Nikodym-style decomposition

$$Du \;=\; \nabla u\,\mathcal{L}^n \;+\; (u^+-u^-)\,\nu_u\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}\restriction J_u \;+\; D^c u,$$

splitting the gradient measure into an absolutely continuous part (the classical $\nabla u\in L^1$), a jump part concentrated on the rectifiable jump set $J_u$ with two-sided traces $u^\pm$ and unit normal $\nu_u$, and a Cantor part $D^c u$ — singular with respect to Lebesgue measure but vanishing on every $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-finite set. The Cantor staircase $u(x)=$ Cantor function has $\nabla u\equiv 0$, no jumps, yet $|Du|([0,1])=1$ — the canonical $\mathrm{BV}\setminus W^{1,1}$ counterexample whose entire variation lives in $D^c u$.

Three properties make $\mathrm{BV}$ the natural setting for variational problems with discontinuities. Lower semicontinuity: if $u_k\to u$ in $L^1$ then $|Du|(\Omega)\le\liminf_k|Du_k|(\Omega)$. Compactness: bounded sequences in $\mathrm{BV}(\Omega)$ have $L^1$-convergent subsequences (a Rellich-type embedding). Coarea: $|Du|(\Omega)=\int_\mathbb{R}|D\chi_{\{u>t\}}|(\Omega)\,dt$ — total variation as integrated level-set perimeter, which is the bridge to §2 and §4.

<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-out');
  const sJ = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-jumps');
  const sJo = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-jumps-out');
  const sA = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-amp');
  const sAo = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-amp-out');
  const sC = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-cantor');
  const sCo = document.getElementById('gmt-bv-cantor-out');
  if(!svg || !out) return;

  // viewBox = -260 -150 520 280; map x in [0,1] to [-220, 220], y values flipped
  const X0 = -220, X1 = 220, Y0 = 100, Y1 = -100;
  const xMap = t => X0 + t * (X1 - X0);
  const yMap = v => Y0 + v * (Y1 - Y0); // v in [0,1]

  // Cantor staircase value at t (depth k)
  function cantor(t, depth){
    if(depth <= 0) return t; // base: identity (smooth fallback)
    let lo = 0, hi = 1, vlo = 0, vhi = 1;
    for(let i = 0; i < depth; i++){
      const a = lo + (hi - lo)/3;
      const b = lo + 2*(hi - lo)/3;
      const vmid = (vlo + vhi)/2;
      if(t < a){ hi = a; vhi = vmid; }
      else if(t > b){ lo = b; vlo = vmid; }
      else { return vmid; }
    }
    // linear interp on the remaining sub-interval (treat as flat at vmid average)
    const span = hi - lo;
    if(span <= 0) return (vlo + vhi)/2;
    return vlo + (t - lo)/span * (vhi - vlo);
  }

  function draw(){
    const N = parseInt(sJ.value, 10);
    const A = parseFloat(sA.value);
    const C = parseFloat(sC.value);
    const cantorDepth = 5;
    sJo.textContent = String(N);
    sAo.textContent = A.toFixed(2);
    sCo.textContent = C.toFixed(2);

    // AC component: smooth ramp 0.4*t  (derivative 0.4)
    const acSlope = 0.4;
    const acTV = acSlope; // ∫_0^1 |0.4| dt = 0.4

    // Jump locations evenly spaced
    const jumps = [];
    for(let i = 1; i <= N; i++){
      jumps.push({ x: i / (N + 1), amp: A });
    }
    const jumpTV = N * Math.abs(A);

    // Cantor part: scaled by C
    const cantorTV = C; // total variation of (C * Cantor) on [0,1] is C

    // Build samples
    const M = 401;
    const xs = new Float64Array(M);
    const ys = new Float64Array(M);
    for(let i = 0; i < M; i++){
      const t = i / (M - 1);
      let v = acSlope * t;
      // jumps
      for(const j of jumps){
        if(t >= j.x) v += j.amp;
      }
      // cantor
      v += C * cantor(t, cantorDepth);
      xs[i] = t;
      ys[i] = v;
    }

    // Normalize y for display: map [vmin, vmax] to [0,1]
    let vmin = Infinity, vmax = -Infinity;
    for(let i = 0; i < M; i++){
      if(ys[i] < vmin) vmin = ys[i];
      if(ys[i] > vmax) vmax = ys[i];
    }
    if(vmax - vmin < 1e-9) vmax = vmin + 1;
    const norm = v => (v - vmin) / (vmax - vmin);

    // Clear SVG (keep <title>)
    while(svg.firstChild){
      if(svg.firstChild.nodeName === 'title') break;
      svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    }
    [...svg.querySelectorAll('g.gmt-bv-layer,path.gmt-bv-line,line.gmt-bv-axis,text.gmt-bv-label,circle.gmt-bv-jump')].forEach(n => n.remove());
    // also nuke residue: simplest, remove every child except <title>
    [...svg.children].forEach(n => { if(n.nodeName !== 'title') svg.removeChild(n); });

    // axes
    const ax = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
    ax.setAttribute('x1', X0); ax.setAttribute('x2', X1);
    ax.setAttribute('y1', Y0); ax.setAttribute('y2', Y0);
    ax.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)'); ax.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
    svg.appendChild(ax);
    const ay = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
    ay.setAttribute('x1', X0); ay.setAttribute('x2', X0);
    ay.setAttribute('y1', Y0); ay.setAttribute('y2', Y1);
    ay.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)'); ay.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
    svg.appendChild(ay);

    // Draw piecewise: the function has discontinuities at jump locations,
    // so draw segments separately so we don't connect across jumps.
    const cuts = [0, ...jumps.map(j => j.x), 1];
    cuts.sort((a,b)=>a-b);
    let segStart = 0;
    for(let s = 0; s < cuts.length - 1; s++){
      const a = cuts[s], b = cuts[s+1];
      const iA = Math.round(a * (M - 1));
      const iB = Math.round(b * (M - 1));
      let d = '';
      // sample from iA up to but not including jump-at-b crossing
      for(let i = iA; i <= iB; i++){
        // Skip the immediate post-jump sample at exactly t = jump.x which already includes jump
        const t = xs[i];
        // Recompute "left side" v for points before next jump: ignore jumps with x === b
        // Simpler: at i = iB exactly, this sample sits at b which already has the jump added.
        // Instead, build the left-limit value:
        let v = acSlope * t;
        for(const j of jumps){
          if(t > j.x || (t === j.x && j.x !== b)) v += j.amp;
        }
        v += C * cantor(t, cantorDepth);
        const X = xMap(t);
        const Y = yMap(norm(v));
        d += (i === iA ? 'M' : 'L') + X.toFixed(2) + ' ' + Y.toFixed(2) + ' ';
      }
      const path = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
      path.setAttribute('d', d.trim());
      path.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
      path.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--cyan)');
      path.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      svg.appendChild(path);
    }

    // Draw jump risers as dashed pink verticals, plus end-point dots
    for(const j of jumps){
      let leftV = acSlope * j.x;
      for(const jj of jumps){ if(jj.x < j.x) leftV += jj.amp; }
      leftV += C * cantor(j.x, cantorDepth);
      const rightV = leftV + j.amp;
      const X = xMap(j.x);
      const Y1p = yMap(norm(leftV));
      const Y2p = yMap(norm(rightV));
      const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ln.setAttribute('x1', X); ln.setAttribute('x2', X);
      ln.setAttribute('y1', Y1p); ln.setAttribute('y2', Y2p);
      ln.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--pink)'); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1.5');
      ln.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '4,3');
      svg.appendChild(ln);
      const c1 = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
      c1.setAttribute('cx', X); c1.setAttribute('cy', Y1p); c1.setAttribute('r', 2.5);
      c1.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--pink)');
      svg.appendChild(c1);
      const c2 = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
      c2.setAttribute('cx', X); c2.setAttribute('cy', Y2p); c2.setAttribute('r', 2.5);
      c2.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--pink)');
      svg.appendChild(c2);
    }

    // axis labels
    const lbl0 = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
    lbl0.setAttribute('x', X0 - 10); lbl0.setAttribute('y', Y0 + 14);
    lbl0.setAttribute('font-size', '11'); lbl0.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
    lbl0.textContent = '0';
    svg.appendChild(lbl0);
    const lbl1 = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
    lbl1.setAttribute('x', X1 - 5); lbl1.setAttribute('y', Y0 + 14);
    lbl1.setAttribute('font-size', '11'); lbl1.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
    lbl1.textContent = '1';
    svg.appendChild(lbl1);

    // Legend
    const lg = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'g');
    lg.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${X0 + 6},${Y1 + 8})`);
    const lgItems = [
      { color: 'var(--cyan)', label: 'u(x) (AC + Cantor + jumps)' },
      { color: 'var(--pink)', label: 'jump risers' },
    ];
    lgItems.forEach((it, i) => {
      const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ln.setAttribute('x1', 0); ln.setAttribute('x2', 18);
      ln.setAttribute('y1', i*14); ln.setAttribute('y2', i*14);
      ln.setAttribute('stroke', it.color); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      lg.appendChild(ln);
      const tx = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
      tx.setAttribute('x', 24); tx.setAttribute('y', i*14 + 4);
      tx.setAttribute('font-size', '11'); tx.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
      tx.textContent = it.label;
      lg.appendChild(tx);
    });
    svg.appendChild(lg);

    const total = acTV + jumpTV + cantorTV;
    out.textContent =
      `|Du|_AC      = ${acTV.toFixed(3)}  (∫|u'_smooth| dt for slope ${acSlope.toFixed(2)})\n` +
      `|Du|_Jump    = ${jumpTV.toFixed(3)}  (${N} jumps × |${A.toFixed(2)}|)\n` +
      `|Du|_Cantor  = ${cantorTV.toFixed(3)}  (Cantor weight ${C.toFixed(2)})\n` +
      `|Du|([0,1])  = ${total.toFixed(3)}`;
  }

  sJ.addEventListener('input', draw);
  sA.addEventListener('input', draw);
  sC.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>

2. Sets of finite perimeter and reduced boundary

A measurable set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ has finite perimeter when $\chi_E\in\mathrm{BV}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and its perimeter is

$$P(E)\;=\;|D\chi_E|(\mathbb{R}^n)\;=\;\sup\Bigl\{\,\int_E\mathrm{div}\,\phi\,dx \,:\, \phi\in C^1_c(\mathbb{R}^n;\mathbb{R}^n),\,|\phi|\le 1\,\Bigr\}.$$

For $E$ with smooth boundary the divergence theorem gives $P(E)=\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\partial E)$, recovering classical surface area. The point of GMT is that this dual definition makes sense — and is finite — for sets whose topological boundary is fractal, has corners, or is wildly non-smooth, while the surface area $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\partial E)$ is sharp only on the reduced part of the boundary.

The reduced boundary $\partial^*E$ is the set of points $x$ where the outward unit normal exists in the measure-theoretic sense:

$$\nu_E(x)\;=\;-\lim_{r\to 0}\frac{D\chi_E(B_r(x))}{|D\chi_E|(B_r(x))} \;\in\; S^{n-1},\qquad |D\chi_E|(B_r(x))>0\text{ for all }r>0.$$

De Giorgi's structure theorem is the central result: if $P(E)<\infty$ then $\partial^*E$ is countably $(n-1)$-rectifiable (a countable union of $C^1$-hypersurface pieces, modulo $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-null), $\nu_E$ is a Borel measurable unit-vector field, $|D\chi_E|=\mathcal{H}^{n-1}\restriction\partial^*E$, and

$$P(E)\;=\;\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\partial^*E),\qquad D\chi_E\;=\;-\nu_E\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}\restriction\partial^*E.$$

This is the divergence theorem extended to corner-y, fractal, and disconnected sets — with the caveat that the topological boundary may be larger than $\partial^*E$. The Koch snowflake is the textbook bad case: it has finite Lebesgue measure but infinite perimeter ($P(E)=\infty$, the limit of perimeters of the pre-fractal approximants), so finite-perimeter regularity forbids it. A square has $\partial^*E$ = the four open edges (the four corners drop out as $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-null — they are the genuinely non-smooth points). The whole isoperimetric story — $P(E)\ge n\omega_n^{1/n}|E|^{(n-1)/n}$ with equality only on balls — lives natively in this class.

      const p1 = [a[0] + dx/3, a[1] + dy/3];
      const p3 = [a[0] + 2*dx/3, a[1] + 2*dy/3];
      // bump outward (right-hand normal of (b-a) with CCW traversal points outward for CW polygon
      // For our drawing y is screen-down so flip):
      const nx = -dy, ny = dx; // perpendicular; choose this direction for outward bump
      const len = Math.hypot(nx, ny) || 1;
      const h = (Math.hypot(dx, dy) / 3) * Math.sqrt(3) / 2;
      const p2 = [(p1[0] + p3[0])/2 + (nx/len) * h, (p1[1] + p3[1])/2 + (ny/len) * h];
      out.push(a, p1, p2, p3);
    }
    return out;
  }

  function polyPerimeter(verts){
    let P = 0;
    for(let i = 0; i < verts.length; i++){
      const a = verts[i];
      const b = verts[(i + 1) % verts.length];
      P += Math.hypot(b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]);
    }
    return P;
  }
  function polyArea(verts){
    let A = 0;
    for(let i = 0; i < verts.length; i++){
      const a = verts[i];
      const b = verts[(i + 1) % verts.length];
      A += a[0] * b[1] - b[0] * a[1];
    }
    return Math.abs(A) / 2;
  }

  function startSquare(){
    // unit square, centered at origin, side length 1.0 in math coords
    return [[-0.5,-0.5],[0.5,-0.5],[0.5,0.5],[-0.5,0.5]];
  }
  function startDisk(){
    const out = [];
    const N = 16;
    for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
      const t = (i / N) * 2 * Math.PI;
      out.push([0.5 * Math.cos(t), 0.5 * Math.sin(t)]);
    }
    return out;
  }

  function draw(){
    const k = parseInt(sD.value, 10);
    sDo.textContent = `k = ${k}`;

    let verts = mode === 'square' ? startSquare() : startDisk();
    const baseP = polyPerimeter(verts);
    const baseA = polyArea(verts);
    for(let i = 0; i < k; i++) verts = kochSubdivide(verts);

    const P = polyPerimeter(verts);
    const A = polyArea(verts);

    // Clear
    [...svg.children].forEach(n => { if(n.nodeName !== 'title') svg.removeChild(n); });

    // Fit polygon into viewBox area: compute bbox, scale to ~340 width
    let xmin = Infinity, xmax = -Infinity, ymin = Infinity, ymax = -Infinity;
    for(const v of verts){
      if(v[0] < xmin) xmin = v[0]; if(v[0] > xmax) xmax = v[0];
      if(v[1] < ymin) ymin = v[1]; if(v[1] > ymax) ymax = v[1];
    }
    const w = xmax - xmin || 1, h = ymax - ymin || 1;
    const scale = Math.min(340 / w, 220 / h);
    const cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2, cy = (ymin + ymax) / 2;
    const proj = v => [(v[0] - cx) * scale, -(v[1] - cy) * scale];
    let d = '';
    verts.forEach((v, i) => {
      const p = proj(v);
      d += (i === 0 ? 'M' : 'L') + p[0].toFixed(2) + ' ' + p[1].toFixed(2) + ' ';
    });
    d += 'Z';
    const path = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
    path.setAttribute('d', d.trim());
    path.setAttribute('fill', 'color-mix(in srgb, var(--violet) 18%, transparent)');
    path.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--violet)');
    path.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1.5');
    path.setAttribute('stroke-linejoin', 'round');
    svg.appendChild(path);

    // Readout
    out.textContent =
      `Refinement depth k = ${k} (${mode})\n` +
      `Perimeter P(E_k) = ${P.toFixed(4)}  (base ${baseP.toFixed(4)}, factor ≈ ${(P/baseP).toFixed(3)} ≈ (4/3)^${k} = ${Math.pow(4/3,k).toFixed(3)})\n` +
      `Area     |E_k|    = ${A.toFixed(4)}  (base ${baseA.toFixed(4)})\n` +
      `As k → ∞: P → ∞, area → finite limit. Koch-type sets fail finite-perimeter.`;
  }

  sD.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>

3. Rectifiable sets and Hausdorff measure

A subset $S\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is countably $k$-rectifiable when $\mathcal{H}^k$-almost all of $S$ is contained in a countable union of Lipschitz images of subsets of $\mathbb{R}^k$:

$$S\;\subset\;S_0\,\cup\,\bigcup_{j=1}^\infty f_j(A_j),\qquad \mathcal{H}^k(S_0)=0,\;f_j:A_j\subset\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ Lipschitz}.$$

This is the geometric measure-theoretic upgrade of "smooth $k$-submanifold up to a measure-zero exceptional set". Three structural facts pin down the class:

Approximate tangent planes. At $\mathcal{H}^k$-almost every $x\in S$ there is a unique $k$-plane $T_xS\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ such that $S$ has density $1$ in $T_xS$ near $x$ (in the precise $r\to 0$ blow-up sense). So rectifiable sets carry a measurable tangent-plane field even when no parameterization is differentiable in the classical sense — a corner point of a Lipschitz curve has tangent direction defined $\mathcal{H}^1$-a.e., just not at the corner itself.

Besicovitch–Federer projection theorem. A purely $k$-unrectifiable set $S$ (no $\mathcal{H}^k$-positive piece is rectifiable) projects to a set of $\mathcal{L}^k$-measure zero on $\mathcal{H}^{k\cdot(n-k)}$-almost every $k$-plane. Rectifiable sets project to positive measure on most planes; purely unrectifiable sets are invisible to most projections. The 2D test: a smooth curve has positive projected length onto almost every line, while the 4-corner Cantor set in the plane projects to a Lebesgue-null set on every line except a Hausdorff-dimension-1 sparse family.

Densities classify. The $k$-dimensional density $\Theta^k(S,x)=\lim_{r\to 0}\mathcal{H}^k(S\cap B_r(x))/(\omega_k r^k)$ exists and equals $1$ at $\mathcal{H}^k$-a.e. point of a rectifiable $S$ (Besicovitch, Marstrand, Mattila). Conversely, $\mathcal{H}^k$-positive sets where the density exists and is positive a.e. are rectifiable. So rectifiability $\Leftrightarrow$ existence of a unit density a.e. — measure-theoretic smoothness reduces to a one-dimensional limit at almost every point.

De Giorgi's structure theorem for finite-perimeter sets is exactly: the reduced boundary is countably $(n-1)$-rectifiable. So §2's $\partial^*E$ is the canonical example of a rectifiable set, and the "surface area equals $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$" identity is a consequence of the density theorem applied to it.

<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('gmt-rect-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('gmt-rect-out');
  const sT = document.getElementById('gmt-rect-theta');
  const sTo = document.getElementById('gmt-rect-theta-out');
  const bC = document.getElementById('gmt-rect-circle');
  const bX = document.getElementById('gmt-rect-cantor');
  if(!svg || !out) return;

  let mode = 'circle';
  function setMode(m){
    mode = m;
    bC.classList.toggle('active', m === 'circle');
    bX.classList.toggle('active', m === 'cantor');
    draw();
  }
  bC.addEventListener('click', () => setMode('circle'));
  bX.addEventListener('click', () => setMode('cantor'));

  // Build 4-corner Cantor set sample points (depth-3, unit square [-0.5,0.5]^2)
  function buildCantor(){
    // start with one cell [(-0.5,-0.5),(0.5,0.5)]
    let cells = [[-0.5,-0.5,0.5,0.5]];
    const depth = 4;
    for(let d = 0; d < depth; d++){
      const next = [];
      for(const c of cells){
        const x0 = c[0], y0 = c[1], x1 = c[2], y1 = c[3];
        const w = (x1 - x0) / 4;
        const h = (y1 - y0) / 4;
        // 4 corner sub-squares: [x0,x0+w] × [y0,y0+h] and the three corners
        next.push([x0, y0, x0 + w, y0 + h]);
        next.push([x1 - w, y0, x1, y0 + h]);
        next.push([x0, y1 - h, x0 + w, y1]);
        next.push([x1 - w, y1 - h, x1, y1]);
      }
      cells = next;
    }
    // Sample center of each cell as a representative point
    return cells.map(c => [(c[0]+c[2])/2, (c[1]+c[3])/2]);
  }
  const cantorPts = buildCantor();

  function buildCirclePts(){
    const pts = [];
    const N = 240;
    for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
      const t = (i / N) * 2 * Math.PI;
      pts.push([0.5 * Math.cos(t), 0.5 * Math.sin(t)]);
    }
    return pts;
  }
  const circlePts = buildCirclePts();

  // Map math units (~[-0.7,0.7]) to screen pixels
  const SCALE = 180;

  function projectionMeasure(pts, theta){
    // project onto unit vector (cos θ, sin θ)
    const u = [Math.cos(theta), Math.sin(theta)];
    const proj = pts.map(p => p[0]*u[0] + p[1]*u[1]);
    proj.sort((a,b)=>a-b);
    if(mode === 'circle'){
      // circle of radius 0.5 projects to interval of length 1 for any θ
      return { min: -0.5, max: 0.5, len: 1.0, occupied: 1.0 };
    } else {
      // For a discrete point cloud sampling the cantor set, count occupied "buckets"
      // bucket size scaled to depth-4: 1/4^depth = 1/256, but we use coarser bins for visibility
      const binW = 1 / 100;
      const min = proj[0], max = proj[proj.length-1];
      const bins = new Set();
      for(const v of proj) bins.add(Math.floor(v / binW));
      const occupied = bins.size * binW;
      return { min, max, len: max - min, occupied };
    }
  }

  function draw(){
    const theta = parseFloat(sT.value);
    sTo.textContent = `θ = ${theta.toFixed(2)} rad (${(theta * 180 / Math.PI).toFixed(0)}°)`;

    const pts = mode === 'circle' ? circlePts : cantorPts;
    const meas = projectionMeasure(pts, theta);

    [...svg.children].forEach(n => { if(n.nodeName !== 'title') svg.removeChild(n); });

    // Draw set on left half (centered at -90, 0 in viewBox coords)
    const setCx = -90, setCy = 0;
    if(mode === 'circle'){
      const c = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
      c.setAttribute('cx', setCx); c.setAttribute('cy', setCy);
      c.setAttribute('r', 0.5 * SCALE);
      c.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
      c.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--cyan)');
      c.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      svg.appendChild(c);
    } else {
      for(const p of cantorPts){
        const dot = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
        dot.setAttribute('cx', setCx + p[0] * SCALE);
        dot.setAttribute('cy', setCy - p[1] * SCALE);
        dot.setAttribute('r', 1);
        dot.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--pink)');
        svg.appendChild(dot);
      }
    }

    // Draw projection direction ray through set center
    const rayLen = 100;
    const ray = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
    ray.setAttribute('x1', setCx - rayLen * Math.cos(theta));
    ray.setAttribute('y1', setCy + rayLen * Math.sin(theta));
    ray.setAttribute('x2', setCx + rayLen * Math.cos(theta));
    ray.setAttribute('y2', setCy - rayLen * Math.sin(theta));
    ray.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--yellow)');
    ray.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
    ray.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '4,3');
    svg.appendChild(ray);

    // Draw projected set on right half (axis horizontal centered at 100, 0)
    const projCx = 100, projCy = 0;
    const axis = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
    axis.setAttribute('x1', projCx - 110); axis.setAttribute('x2', projCx + 110);
    axis.setAttribute('y1', projCy); axis.setAttribute('y2', projCy);
    axis.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)'); axis.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
    svg.appendChild(axis);

    // Project each point of the set onto the axis and place a tick
    const u = [Math.cos(theta), Math.sin(theta)];
    for(const p of pts){
      const v = p[0]*u[0] + p[1]*u[1];
      const tk = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      tk.setAttribute('x1', projCx + v * SCALE);
      tk.setAttribute('x2', projCx + v * SCALE);
      tk.setAttribute('y1', projCy - 8);
      tk.setAttribute('y2', projCy + 8);
      tk.setAttribute('stroke', mode === 'circle' ? 'var(--cyan)' : 'var(--pink)');
      tk.setAttribute('stroke-width', mode === 'circle' ? '0.6' : '0.8');
      tk.setAttribute('opacity', '0.8');
      svg.appendChild(tk);
    }

    // Labels
    const lblL = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
    lblL.setAttribute('x', setCx); lblL.setAttribute('y', setCy + 110);
    lblL.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
    lblL.setAttribute('font-size', '12'); lblL.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
    lblL.textContent = mode === 'circle' ? 'unit circle (rectifiable)' : '4-corner Cantor (purely unrectifiable)';
    svg.appendChild(lblL);

    const lblR = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
    lblR.setAttribute('x', projCx); lblR.setAttribute('y', projCy + 110);
    lblR.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
    lblR.setAttribute('font-size', '12'); lblR.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
    lblR.textContent = `projection onto angle θ = ${theta.toFixed(2)}`;
    svg.appendChild(lblR);

    out.textContent =
      `Mode: ${mode === 'circle' ? 'unit circle (1-rectifiable)' : '4-corner Cantor (purely 1-unrectifiable, dim_H = 1)'}\n` +
      `θ = ${theta.toFixed(3)} rad\n` +
      `H¹(π_θ(S)) ≈ ${meas.occupied.toFixed(4)}  (length of occupied projection)\n` +
      (mode === 'circle'
        ? 'Circle: H¹ of projection = 1 (diameter) for every θ.'
        : 'Cantor: occupied length collapses for almost every θ (Besicovitch–Federer).');
  }

  sT.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>

4. Area and coarea formulas

Two formulas tie together Lipschitz maps, Hausdorff measures, and integration on rectifiable sets. Both hold for Lipschitz $f$ — far broader than $C^1$ — because Rademacher's theorem gives differentiability $\mathcal{L}^k$-almost everywhere.

Area formula. For Lipschitz $f:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^n$ with $k\le n$ and Borel $A\subset\mathbb{R}^k$:

$$\int_A J_f(x)\,d\mathcal{L}^k(x) \;=\; \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \mathcal{H}^0\bigl(A\cap f^{-1}(y)\bigr)\,d\mathcal{H}^k(y),$$

where $J_f(x)=\sqrt{\det(Df(x)^T Df(x))}$ is the $k$-Jacobian. Read right-to-left: integrate the cardinality of preimage fibres against the $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the image, and you recover the Jacobian-weighted Lebesgue integral on the source. When $f$ is injective and $A$ is a parameter region, the right side reduces to $\mathcal{H}^k(f(A))$ and the area formula becomes the classical change-of-variables / surface-area formula: $\mathcal{H}^k(f(A))=\int_A J_f\,d\mathcal{L}^k$. Non-injective $f$ multiply-covers parts of the image; the multiplicity factor $\mathcal{H}^0(A\cap f^{-1}(y))$ is exactly the correction.

Coarea formula. For Lipschitz $u:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ with $m\le n$ and integrable $g$:

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} g(x)\,J_u(x)\,d\mathcal{L}^n(x) \;=\; \int_{\mathbb{R}^m}\Bigl(\int_{u^{-1}(y)} g\,d\mathcal{H}^{n-m}\Bigr)\,d\mathcal{L}^m(y).$$

The level set $u^{-1}(y)$ is $(n-m)$-rectifiable for $\mathcal{L}^m$-a.e. $y$ (the GMT-form of Sard's theorem), and the formula slices a top-dimensional integral by integrating against level-set integrals. The most-cited special case is $m=1$, $g=1$:

$$\int_\Omega |\nabla u|\,dx \;=\; \int_{-\infty}^\infty \mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\Omega\cap\{u=t\})\,dt.$$

Total variation of a smooth $u$ as integrated level-set perimeter — the bridge that, extended to $u\in\mathrm{BV}$, identifies $|Du|(\Omega)=\int|D\chi_{\{u>t\}}|(\Omega)\,dt$ with the integrated perimeter of superlevel sets. Read this as: every BV function is a continuous combination of indicator functions of finite-perimeter sets, weighted by the height of the level. This decomposition is what makes the BV-perimeter equivalence (a Cavalieri-style integration) the operational core of GMT — minimizing $\int|\nabla u|$ over $u$ reduces to simultaneously minimizing $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(\partial^*\{u>t\})$ for almost every $t$.

params.bodyScript:
<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('gmt-coarea-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('gmt-coarea-out');
  const sU = document.getElementById('gmt-coarea-u');
  const sT = document.getElementById('gmt-coarea-t');
  const sTo = document.getElementById('gmt-coarea-t-out');
  if(!svg || !out) return;

  const SCALE = 110; // math unit -> px
  const cx0 = 0, cy0 = 0; // domain center for plotting

  // Each model returns:
  //   levelCurves(t): array of SVG path d-strings to draw {u = t} ∩ unit-disk
  //   H1Level(t): H¹ length of the level set (analytic)
  //   integralAbsGrad(): ∫_{B_1}|∇u| dx
  //   tRange: domain for the t slider (used for Cavalieri sweep)
  function model(name){
    if(name === 'paraboloid'){
      // u = x²+y² ; level set { x²+y² = t } is circle radius √t (only for t ≥ 0).
      return {
        name,
        tRange: [0, 1],
        levelPaths: t => {
          if(t <= 0) return [];
          const r = Math.sqrt(Math.min(t, 1));
          return [arcCirclePath(0, 0, r * SCALE)];
        },
        H1: t => {
          if(t < 0 || t > 1) return 0;
          return 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(t);
        },
        intAbsGrad: () => {
          // ∫_{B_1} 2r * r dr dθ = 2π * 2/3 = 4π/3
          return 4 * Math.PI / 3;
        },
      };
    }
    if(name === 'saddle'){
      // u = x² - y² ; level set is hyperbola pair
      return {
        name,
        tRange: [-1, 1],
        levelPaths: t => {
          // x² - y² = t inside unit disk. Param: y = sinh(s), x = ± cosh(s) * sign? Use t = x²-y²
          // For t > 0: x² = t + y² → x = ±√(t+y²). y ranges so x²+y² ≤ 1.
          // For t < 0: y² = -t + x² → y = ±√(-t+x²). x ranges similarly.
          const paths = [];
          if(Math.abs(t) < 1e-6){
            // two diagonals y = ±x ∩ disk
            paths.push(`M ${(-Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE} ${-(Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE} L ${(Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE} ${(Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE}`);
            paths.push(`M ${(-Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE} ${(Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE} L ${(Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE} ${-(Math.SQRT1_2)*SCALE}`);
            return paths;
          }
          if(t > 0){
            // two branches x = ±√(t+y²)
            for(const sgn of [+1, -1]){
              let d = '';
              let started = false;
              for(let y = -1; y <= 1.001; y += 0.02){
                const x2 = t + y*y;
                if(x2 < 0) continue;
                const x = sgn * Math.sqrt(x2);
                if(x*x + y*y > 1) continue;
                d += (started ? 'L' : 'M') + (x*SCALE).toFixed(2) + ' ' + (-y*SCALE).toFixed(2) + ' ';
                started = true;
              }
              if(d) paths.push(d.trim());
            }
          } else {
            const tt = -t;
            for(const sgn of [+1, -1]){
              let d = '';
              let started = false;
              for(let x = -1; x <= 1.001; x += 0.02){
                const y2 = tt + x*x;
                if(y2 < 0) continue;
                const y = sgn * Math.sqrt(y2);
                if(x*x + y*y > 1) continue;
                d += (started ? 'L' : 'M') + (x*SCALE).toFixed(2) + ' ' + (-y*SCALE).toFixed(2) + ' ';
                started = true;
              }
              if(d) paths.push(d.trim());
            }
          }
          return paths;
        },
        H1: t => {
          // numerical integration along hyperbola arc inside unit disk
          // Arc length element for x²-y² = t: parametrize (x,y) and compute |∂_s|
          // We'll just numerically scan the curve and sum segment lengths.
          if(Math.abs(t) > 1) return 0;
          const eps = 1e-6;
          let total = 0;
          if(Math.abs(t) < eps){
            // length of two chords through origin clipped to disk: each chord is 2 (diameter sqrt(2)*1?)
            // actually y = ±x clipped to x²+y²=1 gives chord length 2 (from (-√½,-√½) to (√½,√½)) = 2*√(2*½) = √2.
            return 2 * Math.sqrt(2);
          }
          if(t > 0){
            for(const sgn of [+1, -1]){
              let prev = null;
              for(let y = -1; y <= 1.0001; y += 0.005){
                const x2 = t + y*y;
                if(x2 < 0) continue;
                const x = sgn * Math.sqrt(x2);
                if(x*x + y*y > 1) continue;
                if(prev) total += Math.hypot(x - prev[0], y - prev[1]);
                prev = [x, y];
              }
            }
          } else {
            const tt = -t;
            for(const sgn of [+1, -1]){
              let prev = null;
              for(let x = -1; x <= 1.0001; x += 0.005){
                const y2 = tt + x*x;
                if(y2 < 0) continue;
                const y = sgn * Math.sqrt(y2);
                if(x*x + y*y > 1) continue;
                if(prev) total += Math.hypot(x - prev[0], y - prev[1]);
                prev = [x, y];
              }
            }
          }
          return total;
        },
        intAbsGrad: () => {
          // |∇u| = 2√(x²+y²) = 2r ; same as paraboloid → 4π/3
          return 4 * Math.PI / 3;
        },
      };
    }
    if(name === 'cone'){
      // u = √(x²+y²) = r ; |∇u| = 1 a.e. (singular at origin); level r=t is circle radius t (t in [0,1])
      return {
        name,
        tRange: [0, 1],
        levelPaths: t => {
          if(t <= 0 || t > 1) return [];
          return [arcCirclePath(0, 0, t * SCALE)];
        },
        H1: t => (t < 0 || t > 1) ? 0 : 2 * Math.PI * t,
        intAbsGrad: () => Math.PI, // ∫_{B_1} 1 dx = π
      };
    }
    if(name === 'ridge'){
      // u = |x|, |∇u| = 1 a.e. on B_1, singular at x=0. Level sets {|x| = t} = two vertical lines
      return {
        name,
        tRange: [0, 1],
        levelPaths: t => {
          if(t <= 0 || t > 1) return [];
          const yMax = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 - t*t));
          // vertical chords at x = ±t inside unit disk
          return [
            `M ${(t*SCALE).toFixed(2)} ${(-yMax*SCALE).toFixed(2)} L ${(t*SCALE).toFixed(2)} ${(yMax*SCALE).toFixed(2)}`,
            `M ${(-t*SCALE).toFixed(2)} ${(-yMax*SCALE).toFixed(2)} L ${(-t*SCALE).toFixed(2)} ${(yMax*SCALE).toFixed(2)}`,
          ];
        },
        H1: t => {
          if(t < 0 || t > 1) return 0;
          // Two chords each of length 2√(1-t²)
          return 4 * Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, 1 - t*t));
        },
        intAbsGrad: () => Math.PI, // ∫_{B_1} 1 = π
      };
    }
    return null;
  }

  function arcCirclePath(cx, cy, r){
    if(r <= 0.5) return `M ${(cx+r).toFixed(2)} ${cy} A ${r.toFixed(2)} ${r.toFixed(2)} 0 1 0 ${(cx-r).toFixed(2)} ${cy} A ${r.toFixed(2)} ${r.toFixed(2)} 0 1 0 ${(cx+r).toFixed(2)} ${cy}`;
    return `M ${(cx+r).toFixed(2)} ${cy} A ${r.toFixed(2)} ${r.toFixed(2)} 0 1 0 ${(cx-r).toFixed(2)} ${cy} A ${r.toFixed(2)} ${r.toFixed(2)} 0 1 0 ${(cx+r).toFixed(2)} ${cy}`;
  }

  function cavalieriSum(m, N){
    // Riemann sum of H¹(u^{-1}(t)) over t in tRange with N subintervals (skipping singular t)
    const [a, b] = m.tRange;
    const dt = (b - a) / N;
    let sum = 0;
    for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
      const t = a + (i + 0.5) * dt;
      const v = m.H1(t);
      if(Number.isFinite(v)) sum += v * dt;
    }
    return sum;
  }

  function draw(){
    const name = sU.value;
    const m = model(name);
    const t = parseFloat(sT.value);
    sTo.textContent = `t = ${t.toFixed(2)}`;

    [...svg.children].forEach(n => { if(n.nodeName !== 'title') svg.removeChild(n); });

    // Draw unit disk outline
    const disk = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
    disk.setAttribute('cx', cx0); disk.setAttribute('cy', cy0);
    disk.setAttribute('r', SCALE);
    disk.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
    disk.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)');
    disk.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
    disk.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '3,3');
    svg.appendChild(disk);

    // Background gradient field via subsampled streamlines (just a hint of |∇u| variation)
    // Skip for clarity; instead show a faint contour at several t values.
    for(let tt = m.tRange[0] + 0.1; tt <= m.tRange[1] - 0.05; tt += 0.2){
      for(const dStr of m.levelPaths(tt)){
        const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
        p.setAttribute('d', dStr);
        p.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
        p.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)');
        p.setAttribute('stroke-width', '0.8');
        p.setAttribute('opacity', '0.55');
        svg.appendChild(p);
      }
    }

    // Highlighted level set at current t
    for(const dStr of m.levelPaths(t)){
      const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
      p.setAttribute('d', dStr);
      p.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
      p.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--yellow)');
      p.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2.4');
      svg.appendChild(p);
    }

    const H1t = m.H1(t);
    const N = 64;
    const cavSum = cavalieriSum(m, N);
    const trueIntegral = m.intAbsGrad();

    out.textContent =
      `u(x,y) = ${({paraboloid:'x²+y²', saddle:'x²-y²', cone:'√(x²+y²)', ridge:'|x|'})[name]}\n` +
      `Level set u⁻¹(${t.toFixed(2)}) ∩ B₁: H¹ ≈ ${H1t.toFixed(4)}\n` +
      `Cavalieri sum  ∫ H¹(u⁻¹(t)) dt  (N=${N}) ≈ ${cavSum.toFixed(4)}\n` +
      `∫_{B₁} |∇u| dx (analytic)            = ${trueIntegral.toFixed(4)}\n` +
      `coarea identity: the two should match (small N introduces discretization error).`;
  }

  sU.addEventListener('change', draw);
  sT.addEventListener('input', draw);
  // also handle the katex-select shim button changes via same change event on hidden select
  draw();
})();
</script>

5. Currents and Federer–Fleming compactness

De Rham's currents generalize oriented submanifolds the way distributions generalize functions: a $k$-current $T$ is a continuous linear functional on the space $\mathcal{D}^k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of smooth, compactly supported $k$-forms. An oriented $k$-submanifold $M$ defines its integration current $[M]$ by

$$\langle [M],\omega\rangle \;=\; \int_M\omega,\qquad\omega\in\mathcal{D}^k(\mathbb{R}^n).$$

Currents have a boundary: $\partial T$ is the $(k-1)$-current with $\langle\partial T,\eta\rangle=\langle T,d\eta\rangle$. For an integration current $[M]$ this recovers Stokes' theorem: $\partial[M]=[\partial M]$. Currents have a mass

$$\mathbf{M}(T)\;=\;\sup\bigl\{\,\langle T,\omega\rangle\,:\,\omega\in\mathcal{D}^k,\,\|\omega\|_\infty\le 1\,\bigr\},$$

which generalizes $\mathcal{H}^k$-measure: $\mathbf{M}([M])=\mathcal{H}^k(M)$ for an oriented submanifold. The class of integral currents $\mathbf{I}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ consists of locally rectifiable $k$-currents $T$ (carried by an $\mathcal{H}^k$-rectifiable set with integer-valued multiplicity and $\mathcal{H}^k$-measurable orientation) for which $\partial T$ is itself locally rectifiable. They are the GMT replacement for oriented Lipschitz chains.

Federer–Fleming compactness theorem. Let $\{T_j\}\subset\mathbf{I}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be a sequence with $\mathrm{spt}(T_j)\subset K$ (a fixed compact set) and uniform bounds $\mathbf{M}(T_j)+\mathbf{M}(\partial T_j)\le C$. Then there is a subsequence $T_{j_l}$ converging weakly (i.e., $\langle T_{j_l},\omega\rangle\to\langle T,\omega\rangle$ for every $\omega\in\mathcal{D}^k$) to an integral current $T\in\mathbf{I}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with $\mathbf{M}(T)\le\liminf\mathbf{M}(T_{j_l})$ and $\mathbf{M}(\partial T)\le\liminf\mathbf{M}(\partial T_{j_l})$.

This is the engine of GMT existence theory. Compactness in classical function spaces (Arzelà-Ascoli on $C^0$, Rellich on $W^{1,p}$) cannot extract a limit from a minimizing sequence of surfaces: equiboundedness in $\mathcal{H}^k$ alone is too weak, and the limit can fail to be a manifold. Integral currents — measure-theoretic generalized surfaces with quantized multiplicity — form a class large enough to be closed under weak limits of mass-bounded minimizing sequences and small enough to retain a coherent boundary calculus. The Plateau-problem proof is now mechanical: take a minimizing sequence of currents with prescribed boundary, extract a weakly convergent subsequence by Federer-Fleming, and the limit minimizes mass.

<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('gmt-currents-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('gmt-currents-out');
  const bAdd = document.getElementById('gmt-currents-add');
  const bClear = document.getElementById('gmt-currents-clear');
  const bLoop = document.getElementById('gmt-currents-loop');
  if(!svg || !out) return;

  // segments: array of {from:[x,y], to:[x,y]} in viewBox coords
  let segments = [];
  let pending = null; // first click is the tail; second click is the head

  function clear(){
    segments = [];
    pending = null;
    redraw();
  }
  bClear.addEventListener('click', clear);

  bAdd.addEventListener('click', () => {
    bAdd.classList.add('active');
  });

  bLoop.addEventListener('click', () => {
    // add a closed triangle near the center; ∂T should cancel
    const cx = 0, cy = 0, r = 60;
    const A = [cx + r, cy + 0];
    const B = [cx - r/2, cy - r * Math.sqrt(3)/2];
    const C = [cx - r/2, cy + r * Math.sqrt(3)/2];
    segments.push({ from: A, to: B });
    segments.push({ from: B, to: C });
    segments.push({ from: C, to: A });
    pending = null;
    redraw();
  });

  // Convert pointer event to viewBox coordinates
  function ptInVB(evt){
    const pt = svg.createSVGPoint();
    pt.x = evt.clientX;
    pt.y = evt.clientY;
    const ctm = svg.getScreenCTM();
    if(!ctm) return null;
    const v = pt.matrixTransform(ctm.inverse());
    return [v.x, v.y];
  }

  svg.addEventListener('click', (evt) => {
    const p = ptInVB(evt);
    if(!p) return;
    if(!pending){
      pending = p;
    } else {
      segments.push({ from: pending, to: p });
      pending = null;
    }
    redraw();
  });

  function vertexKey(p){
    // bucket nearby endpoints together to detect cancellation
    const k = 6; // px snap radius
    return `${Math.round(p[0]/k)},${Math.round(p[1]/k)}`;
  }

  function boundaryAndMass(){
    // mass = sum of segment lengths
    // ∂T at each vertex = (incoming - outgoing) signed multiplicity
    const tally = new Map(); // key -> { x, y, count }
    let mass = 0;
    for(const s of segments){
      const dx = s.to[0] - s.from[0], dy = s.to[1] - s.from[1];
      mass += Math.hypot(dx, dy);
      // tail contributes -1; head contributes +1
      const kFrom = vertexKey(s.from);
      const kTo = vertexKey(s.to);
      if(!tally.has(kFrom)) tally.set(kFrom, { x: s.from[0], y: s.from[1], count: 0 });
      tally.get(kFrom).count -= 1;
      if(!tally.has(kTo)) tally.set(kTo, { x: s.to[0], y: s.to[1], count: 0 });
      tally.get(kTo).count += 1;
    }
    let bdyMass = 0;
    const verts = [];
    for(const v of tally.values()){
      if(v.count !== 0){
        bdyMass += Math.abs(v.count);
        verts.push(v);
      }
    }
    return { mass, bdyMass, verts };
  }

  function redraw(){
    [...svg.children].forEach(n => { if(n.nodeName !== 'title') svg.removeChild(n); });

    // arrow marker
    const defs = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'defs');
    const mkP = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'marker');
    mkP.setAttribute('id', 'gmt-cur-arrow');
    mkP.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 10 10');
    mkP.setAttribute('refX', '9'); mkP.setAttribute('refY', '5');
    mkP.setAttribute('markerWidth', '5'); mkP.setAttribute('markerHeight', '5');
    mkP.setAttribute('orient', 'auto');
    const mkPath = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
    mkPath.setAttribute('d', 'M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z');
    mkPath.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--cyan)');
    mkP.appendChild(mkPath);
    defs.appendChild(mkP);
    svg.appendChild(defs);

    // light grid
    for(let gx = -240; gx <= 240; gx += 60){
      const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ln.setAttribute('x1', gx); ln.setAttribute('x2', gx);
      ln.setAttribute('y1', -130); ln.setAttribute('y2', 130);
      ln.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)'); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '0.4');
      svg.appendChild(ln);
    }
    for(let gy = -120; gy <= 120; gy += 60){
      const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ln.setAttribute('x1', -240); ln.setAttribute('x2', 240);
      ln.setAttribute('y1', gy); ln.setAttribute('y2', gy);
      ln.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)'); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '0.4');
      svg.appendChild(ln);
    }

    // segments
    for(const s of segments){
      const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ln.setAttribute('x1', s.from[0]); ln.setAttribute('y1', s.from[1]);
      ln.setAttribute('x2', s.to[0]); ln.setAttribute('y2', s.to[1]);
      ln.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--cyan)'); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      ln.setAttribute('marker-end', 'url(#gmt-cur-arrow)');
      svg.appendChild(ln);
    }

    // pending tail marker
    if(pending){
      const c = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
      c.setAttribute('cx', pending[0]); c.setAttribute('cy', pending[1]);
      c.setAttribute('r', 4);
      c.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--yellow)');
      svg.appendChild(c);
    }

    // boundary tally as filled circles
    const { mass, bdyMass, verts } = boundaryAndMass();
    for(const v of verts){
      const r = 3 + Math.min(Math.abs(v.count) * 1.5, 8);
      const c = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
      c.setAttribute('cx', v.x); c.setAttribute('cy', v.y);
      c.setAttribute('r', r);
      c.setAttribute('fill', v.count > 0 ? 'var(--green)' : 'var(--pink)');
      c.setAttribute('opacity', '0.8');
      svg.appendChild(c);
      const t = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
      t.setAttribute('x', v.x + r + 4); t.setAttribute('y', v.y + 3);
      t.setAttribute('font-size', '10'); t.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
      t.textContent = (v.count > 0 ? '+' : '') + v.count;
      svg.appendChild(t);
    }

    out.textContent =
      `Segments: ${segments.length}` + (pending ? '  (waiting for head — click again)' : '') + '\n' +
      `Mass M(T)         = ${mass.toFixed(2)}  (px; sum of segment lengths)\n` +
      `Boundary mass M(∂T) = ${bdyMass.toFixed(2)}  (sum |signed multiplicities|)\n` +
      (bdyMass === 0 && segments.length > 0
        ? '∂T = 0 — closed cycle (Federer–Fleming weak limit class).'
        : '∂T ≠ 0 — open chain. Adding closing edges cancels endpoints.');
  }

  redraw();
})();
</script>

6. Applications: Plateau, minimal surfaces, and Mumford–Shah

Three flagship arenas where GMT replaces ad-hoc PDE / variational tools with a uniform existence theorem:

Plateau's problem. Given a closed $(k-1)$-current $\Gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with finite mass, find a $k$-current $T$ with $\partial T=\Gamma$ minimizing mass — the higher-dimensional soap-film problem. Federer-Fleming (§5) does the heavy lifting: a minimizing sequence $T_j$ has uniformly bounded mass (any competitor is an upper bound) and fixed boundary mass $\mathbf{M}(\Gamma)$; pass to a weakly convergent subsequence with limit $T$ satisfying $\partial T=\Gamma$ and $\mathbf{M}(T)=\inf$. Existence is mechanical.

Regularity is delicate, and clean statements need a slightly larger object than a current. A varifold is a Radon measure on the Grassmannian bundle $\mathbb{R}^n\times G(n,k)$ — informally, a current with orientation forgotten but tangent-plane data retained. Currents lose embedded-vs-immersed information (a soap film that self-touches has $\partial T=\Gamma$ degenerate to nothing meaningful at the contact); varifolds keep the unsigned mass and the tangent-plane field. An integral varifold is the rectifiable, integer-multiplicity sub-class. A varifold is stationary when the first variation of mass under any compactly-supported diffeomorphism vanishes — the variational analogue of vanishing mean curvature. Allard's regularity theorem says the support of a stationary integral varifold is a $C^{1,\alpha}$-submanifold $\mathcal{H}^k$-almost everywhere. A celebrated chain of results (Fleming, De Giorgi, Almgren, Simons) shows that codimension-1 minimizers are $C^\infty$ in dimensions $n\le 7$, with the Simons cone $\{x_1^2+\cdots+x_4^2=x_5^2+\cdots+x_8^2\}$ giving the first singular minimizer in $\mathbb{R}^8$.

Mumford-Shah image segmentation. The functional

$$\mathcal{E}(u,K)\;=\;\int_{\Omega\setminus K}(u-g)^2\,dx \;+\;\alpha\int_{\Omega\setminus K}|\nabla u|^2\,dx\;+\;\beta\,\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(K)$$

is minimized over pairs $(u,K)$ with $K\subset\Omega$ a closed singular set and $u\in C^1(\Omega\setminus K)$: a piecewise-smooth approximation $u$ to the noisy data $g$, paired with an edge set $K$ whose total $(n-1)$-measure is penalized. Direct minimization on closed-set pairs fails because the obvious topology on closed sets is bad — Hausdorff convergence does not control $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$. The fix is to lift $K$ into the BV decomposition. Special BV functions $\mathrm{SBV}(\Omega)$ are the subspace of $\mathrm{BV}(\Omega)$ cut out by $D^c u=0$: only the absolutely-continuous and jump parts survive, with $K=J_u$ then a rectifiable jump set. Ambrosio's SBV compactness theorem (1989) is the version of Federer-Fleming for this class: bounded sequences in SBV with bounded $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}(J_u)$ have $L^1$-convergent subsequences whose limit lies in SBV with the diffuse Cantor singularities zero'd out — exactly what makes Mumford-Shah well-posed. De Giorgi-Carriero-Leaci then close the singular set $K=\overline{J_u}$ via density estimates: GMT making a computer-vision functional rigorous.

Mean-curvature flow and Cheeger inequalities. A Brakke flow is a weak solution of mean-curvature flow defined as a one-parameter family $\{V_t\}$ of varifolds whose mass decreases at the squared mean curvature: $\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{M}(V_t)\le -\int|H|^2\,dV_t$. Past pinch-off / topology-change singularities the smooth flow ceases to make sense; the varifold formulation continues. The Cheeger constant $h(\Omega)=\inf_E P(E)/\min(|E|,|\Omega\setminus E|)$ — a perimeter-volume isoperimetric quotient — gives the Cheeger inequality $\lambda_1(\Omega)\ge h(\Omega)^2/4$, an isoperimetric lower bound on the Laplacian spectral gap. Cheeger uses the coarea bridge directly (level-set perimeter argument); Brakke flow uses varifold tangent-measure rectifiability and Allard-style regularity rather than coarea.

<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-out');
  const bP = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-plateau');
  const bM = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-ms');
  const sN = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-noise');
  const sNo = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-noise-out');
  const sB = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-beta');
  const sBo = document.getElementById('gmt-plat-beta-out');
  if(!svg || !out) return;

  let mode = 'plateau';
  function setMode(m){
    mode = m;
    bP.classList.toggle('active', m === 'plateau');
    bM.classList.toggle('active', m === 'ms');
    draw();
  }
  bP.addEventListener('click', () => setMode('plateau'));
  bM.addEventListener('click', () => setMode('ms'));

  // Generate ground-truth signal (3-step staircase) plus noise
  const N = 80;
  function buildSignal(noise){
    // staircase: levels 0.2 on [0,30), 0.7 on [30,55), 0.4 on [55, 80)
    // Use a deterministic pseudo-RNG so results are reproducible per noise level
    const g = new Float64Array(N);
    let seed = 1234567;
    function rand(){
      seed = (seed * 1664525 + 1013904223) | 0;
      return ((seed >>> 0) / 0xffffffff) - 0.5;
    }
    for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
      let v;
      if(i < 30) v = 0.2;
      else if(i < 55) v = 0.7;
      else v = 0.4;
      v += noise * rand() * 2;
      g[i] = v;
    }
    return g;
  }

  // Mumford-Shah-on-1D dynamic program.
  // J(i) = min over j < i of [ J(j) + segCost(j+1, i) ] + β if j ≥ 0
  // segCost(a,b) = sum_{k=a..b} (g[k] - mean_{a..b})^2
  // ground state J(-1) = 0 ; result builds optimal break-set.
  function runDP(g, beta){
    const n = g.length;
    // prefix sums for O(1) variance
    const ps = new Float64Array(n + 1);
    const ps2 = new Float64Array(n + 1);
    for(let i = 0; i < n; i++){
      ps[i+1] = ps[i] + g[i];
      ps2[i+1] = ps2[i] + g[i]*g[i];
    }
    function segCost(a, b){
      // [a, b] inclusive, length L = b - a + 1
      const L = b - a + 1;
      if(L <= 0) return 0;
      const sum = ps[b+1] - ps[a];
      const sumSq = ps2[b+1] - ps2[a];
      const mean = sum / L;
      const cost = sumSq - L * mean * mean;
      return Math.max(0, cost);
    }
    // J[i] = best cost ending at index i (segment last contains i)
    // back[i] = the start index of the last segment
    const J = new Float64Array(n);
    const back = new Int32Array(n);
    for(let i = 0; i < n; i++){
      let best = Infinity, bestStart = 0;
      for(let a = 0; a <= i; a++){
        const prev = (a === 0) ? 0 : (J[a-1] + beta); // each break costs β
        const c = segCost(a, i) + prev;
        if(c < best){ best = c; bestStart = a; }
      }
      J[i] = best;
      back[i] = bestStart;
    }
    // backtrack
    const breaks = [];
    let cur = n - 1;
    while(cur >= 0){
      const start = back[cur];
      if(start > 0) breaks.unshift(start);
      cur = start - 1;
    }
    // segment-wise mean signal u
    const u = new Float64Array(n);
    let segStart = 0;
    const segEdges = [...breaks, n];
    for(const e of segEdges){
      const a = segStart, b = e - 1;
      let s = 0;
      for(let k = a; k <= b; k++) s += g[k];
      const mean = s / (b - a + 1);
      for(let k = a; k <= b; k++) u[k] = mean;
      segStart = e;
    }
    return { J, breaks, u };
  }

  function draw(){
    const noise = parseFloat(sN.value);
    const beta = parseFloat(sB.value);
    sNo.textContent = noise.toFixed(2);
    sBo.textContent = beta.toFixed(2);

    [...svg.children].forEach(n => { if(n.nodeName !== 'title') svg.removeChild(n); });

    // viewBox: -260 -150 520 280
    const X0 = -220, X1 = 220, Y0 = 100, Y1 = -100;
    const xMap = i => X0 + (i / (N - 1)) * (X1 - X0);

    if(mode === 'plateau'){
      // 2D: render two boundary points and the chord (the linear length-minimizer).
      // Show that the "minimal connecting chain" with given boundary is the straight segment.
      const A = [-130, 60], B = [140, -50];
      const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ln.setAttribute('x1', A[0]); ln.setAttribute('y1', A[1]);
      ln.setAttribute('x2', B[0]); ln.setAttribute('y2', B[1]);
      ln.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--cyan)'); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      svg.appendChild(ln);
      // Wiggly competitor (longer)
      let d = `M ${A[0]} ${A[1]}`;
      const seg = 12;
      for(let i = 1; i <= seg; i++){
        const t = i / seg;
        const x = A[0] + t * (B[0] - A[0]);
        const y = A[1] + t * (B[1] - A[1]) + 30 * Math.sin(t * Math.PI * 3);
        d += ` L ${x.toFixed(1)} ${y.toFixed(1)}`;
      }
      const wig = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
      wig.setAttribute('d', d);
      wig.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
      wig.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--mute)');
      wig.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1.2');
      wig.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '4,3');
      svg.appendChild(wig);
      for(const P of [A, B]){
        const c = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
        c.setAttribute('cx', P[0]); c.setAttribute('cy', P[1]);
        c.setAttribute('r', 4);
        c.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--pink)');
        svg.appendChild(c);
      }
      const lbl = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
      lbl.setAttribute('x', 0); lbl.setAttribute('y', -110);
      lbl.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
      lbl.setAttribute('font-size', '12'); lbl.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
      lbl.textContent = 'Plateau in 2D: minimize length over chains with boundary {A, B}';
      svg.appendChild(lbl);
      const massStraight = Math.hypot(B[0]-A[0], B[1]-A[1]);
      // estimate wiggly length
      let wL = 0; let prev = A;
      for(let i = 1; i <= seg; i++){
        const t = i / seg;
        const x = A[0] + t * (B[0] - A[0]);
        const y = A[1] + t * (B[1] - A[1]) + 30 * Math.sin(t * Math.PI * 3);
        wL += Math.hypot(x - prev[0], y - prev[1]); prev = [x, y];
      }
      out.textContent =
        `Plateau (2D, k=1): minimize mass over 1-currents with ∂T = δ_B − δ_A.\n` +
        `Straight segment (cyan): mass M = ${massStraight.toFixed(2)} px (the unique minimizer).\n` +
        `Wiggly competitor (dashed): mass M = ${wL.toFixed(2)} px.\n` +
        `Federer–Fleming guarantees a weakly-convergent minimizing subsequence; here it converges to the chord.`;
    } else {
      const g = buildSignal(noise);
      const { breaks, u } = runDP(g, beta);

      // axis
      const ax = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ax.setAttribute('x1', X0); ax.setAttribute('x2', X1);
      ax.setAttribute('y1', Y0 + 6); ax.setAttribute('y2', Y0 + 6);
      ax.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--line)'); ax.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
      svg.appendChild(ax);

      // map signal value [vmin, vmax] to [Y0, Y1]
      let vmin = Infinity, vmax = -Infinity;
      for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
        if(g[i] < vmin) vmin = g[i];
        if(g[i] > vmax) vmax = g[i];
        if(u[i] < vmin) vmin = u[i];
        if(u[i] > vmax) vmax = u[i];
      }
      if(vmax - vmin < 1e-6) vmax = vmin + 1;
      const yMap = v => Y0 - ((v - vmin) / (vmax - vmin)) * (Y0 - Y1);

      // raw signal as small dots
      for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
        const dot = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
        dot.setAttribute('cx', xMap(i)); dot.setAttribute('cy', yMap(g[i]));
        dot.setAttribute('r', 1.6);
        dot.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
        svg.appendChild(dot);
      }
      // segmented u as step function (cyan)
      let dStr = '';
      for(let i = 0; i < N; i++){
        const x = xMap(i);
        const y = yMap(u[i]);
        // draw horizontal then vertical at break
        if(i === 0){ dStr += `M ${x.toFixed(1)} ${y.toFixed(1)}`; }
        else {
          const xPrev = xMap(i-1);
          if(u[i] !== u[i-1]){
            dStr += ` L ${x.toFixed(1)} ${yMap(u[i-1]).toFixed(1)}`;
          }
          dStr += ` L ${x.toFixed(1)} ${y.toFixed(1)}`;
        }
      }
      const path = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
      path.setAttribute('d', dStr);
      path.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
      path.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--cyan)');
      path.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      svg.appendChild(path);
      // edges (vertical pink dashed at each break)
      for(const k of breaks){
        const x = xMap(k);
        const ln = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
        ln.setAttribute('x1', x); ln.setAttribute('x2', x);
        ln.setAttribute('y1', Y1); ln.setAttribute('y2', Y0);
        ln.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--pink)'); ln.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1');
        ln.setAttribute('stroke-dasharray', '3,3');
        svg.appendChild(ln);
      }

      // legend
      const lblL = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
      lblL.setAttribute('x', X0); lblL.setAttribute('y', Y1 - 4);
      lblL.setAttribute('font-size', '11'); lblL.setAttribute('fill', 'var(--mute)');
      lblL.textContent = `noisy signal g (mute) | recovered piecewise-constant u (cyan) | edge set K = J_u (pink dashed)`;
      svg.appendChild(lblL);

      const fidelity = (() => { let s = 0; for(let i = 0; i < N; i++) s += (u[i]-g[i])*(u[i]-g[i]); return s; })();
      out.textContent =
        `Mode: Mumford–Shah (1D) on N=${N} samples; noise σ ≈ ${noise.toFixed(2)}; β = ${beta.toFixed(2)}.\n` +
        `DP recovered K = J_u at indices [${breaks.join(', ')}]  (|K| = ${breaks.length})\n` +
        `Energy ≈ Σ(u−g)² + β·|K| = ${fidelity.toFixed(3)} + ${(beta*breaks.length).toFixed(3)} = ${(fidelity + beta*breaks.length).toFixed(3)}\n` +
        `Ground truth has 2 internal jumps at i=30 and i=55 — increase β to merge spurious edges, decrease to over-segment.`;
    }
  }

  sN.addEventListener('input', draw);
  sB.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>

Connections

Geometric measure theory is the analytic toolkit for problems where the natural class of competitors is rougher than smooth submanifolds: minimal surfaces with corners, BV functions with jumps, edge sets in noisy images, fractal boundary phenomena. Open frontiers include the regularity of solutions to higher-codimension Plateau problems (Almgren's $Q$-valued functions, the De Lellis-Spadaro program), GMT on metric measure spaces (Cheeger differentiation, Ambrosio-Kirchheim currents in metric spaces, Heisenberg-group GMT), the Mumford-Shah conjecture on the regularity of singular sets in image segmentation, and Brakke-flow weak solutions for mean-curvature flow past singularities. Below the headline names, the field is still actively producing new compactness theorems for variant function classes (BD, GSBV, GBD).

  • Measure theory — Hausdorff measure & dimension — supplies $\mathcal{H}^k$, the substrate for rectifiability, currents, and the area / coarea formulas. The s-dimensional Hausdorff measure introduced there becomes the unit of mass for integration currents and the way perimeter is even defined.
  • Sobolev spaces & distributions — distributional / weak derivatives — the BV space sits one rung above $W^{1,1}$: the gradient is a Radon measure (allowing jumps and Cantor parts) rather than an $L^1$ function. Section 1's BV decomposition is exactly the Radon-Nikodym refinement of the distributional derivative.
  • Real analysis — bounded variation — the 1D classical $\mathrm{BV}([a,b])$ via Jordan's monotone-difference theorem is the point of departure. GMT's BV is the multivariable measure-valued upgrade, and the Cantor function reappears here as the canonical $\mathrm{BV}\setminus\mathrm{AC}$ counterexample.
  • Differential forms — Stokes & de Rham — currents are the distributional dual of compactly-supported smooth forms, and Stokes' theorem $\partial[M]=[\partial M]$ is built into the very definition of $\partial T$ on currents. Federer-Fleming's existence theorem is essentially de Rham's theory done with rectifiable carriers and integer multiplicities.
  • Variational methods — direct method — every existence theorem in §6 (Plateau, Mumford-Shah) is the direct method of the calculus of variations carried out in a function class (currents, SBV) chosen so that the requisite lower semicontinuity + compactness pair both hold. GMT is what enables the direct method to land outside Sobolev space.
  • Atiyah-Singer index theorem — Allard's regularity theorem and the regularity theory of minimal currents lean on elliptic estimates for the linearization of the area functional; the geometric-analytic regularity story for stationary varifolds is in the same intellectual neighborhood as parametrix-driven regularity in microlocal analysis.
